findings.description: 預けた means entrusted or deposited deeds and authorization. WH signed over suggests a completed transfer of rights rather than the risky document arrangement.

contexts.japanese:
「………権利書と委任状を預けた…」
「それは…、どういう意味ですか……」
恐らく蔵臼の言うそれは、財産を実質的に相手に預けたというのと同じ意味だろう。
担保ならば、まだ法律に基づいたやり取りも可能だ。
相手は少なくとも銀行で、温情は一切ないだろうが、
社会的なルールの範囲内で話を進めることが出来る。
……しかし、権利書と委任状を預けるのは、その段階を遥かに超える。
つまり、蔵臼たちが今、こうして住んでいる屋敷でさえ。
権利書を持つ人物が、蔵臼との取り決めを一方的に無視して、今すぐこの瞬間に第三者に転売したとしても、何も咎めることが出来ない。
借金の担保どころか、家を売ってお金を借りているも同然の状態なのだ…。
「…つまり、…右代宮家の生殺与奪は、金貸したちの手に委ねられていたわけですね。
彼らがほんの僅かの気紛れを起こして、突然、この家を売り払ったら。
……私たちは今すぐにも荷物をまとめ、出て行かなくてはならないということですね…？」
「理屈上はそうだ。
だが、取引の相手はいずれも社会的信用のある人物ばかりだ。
サラ金じゃないぞ。
経済人同士の信用取引だ」
「私も相手を信用している。
相手だって、私に金を貸すことで私が大きな事業を成功させ、投資した額が大きくなって返ってくることを信用している。
委任状を預けたのは、私の誠意と事業の絶対の成功を疑わないからだ」

contexts.WH: ".........I signed over the deeds and power of attorney..."
contexts.MG:
"......I signed over the deeds and power of attorney..."
"And...what does that mean...?"
What Krauss was saying probably meant that he had, in essence, signed away the rights to his assets.
If these assets had been used as collateral for a loan, then Krauss would still have some leeway under the law.
He would have to deal with a bank, which would have absolutely no compassion,
but they would be able to work something out within the rules set by society.
...However, signing away the deed and power of attorney was a whole different story.
In other words, even the mansion they were living in.
If the person holding the deed were to decide to ignore his agreement with Krauss...and sell the mansion to a third party right this moment, they would have no recourse whatsoever.
Far from using collateral for a loan, this was basically the same as selling their house to borrow money...
"...In other words, ...the moneylenders have the power to make or break the Ushiromiya family as they please.
If they were to suddenly sell our house on some slight whim,
......we'd have to pack our bags and leave right now, wouldn't we...?"
"That is technically true.
However, everyone I have had dealings with is very reputable.
This isn't consumer financing.
It's a transaction based on trust between economically literate men."
"I trust them.
And they, in turn, trust that by lending me money, I will achieve great success in business and give them massive returns on their investment.
I signed over the power of attorney as a sign of good faith and so that they wouldn't have to doubt in the certain success of my business.

findings.sourceReading: 囁き合っていたという reports that elders whispered he might have hit his head and returned changed (のではないか). Both reporting layers qualify the explanation.
findings.alternative: Must have can indicate conjecture rather than certainty, and whispering marks informal judgment. Even so, it strengthens the conjecture and omits narrator hearsay qualification.

findings.sourceReading: Doubt is transitive in this construction; success is its direct object.
findings.alternative: Doubt in can occur in unusual literary constructions, but here it blends doubt something with have doubts about something and produces faulty ordinary prose.

findings.description: WH shifts the already catastrophic condition into a hypothetical future worst event.

contexts.japanesePS3: この屋敷さえも、明日には立ち退けと命じられても拒めぬという最悪の状況です。
contexts.WH: "Yes.  If the worst happens and we are ordered to leave this mansion tomorrow, we won't be able to refuse.  During the distribution of the inheritance, the relatives might even file a criminal complaint."
contexts.MG: If the worst happens and we are ordered to leave this mansion tomorrow, we won't be able to refuse.
contexts.UP: Things could hardly be worse—we could even be ordered to leave this mansion tomorrow, and we wouldn't be able to refuse.

MG.japanese: 「はい。この屋敷さえも、明日には立ち退けと命じられても拒めぬという最悪の状況です。遺産分配となれば、親族たちに刑事告発さえされるかもしれません」

findings.description: UP replaces reluctantly agreeing to a deal he cannot refuse with being unable to pass up a deal.

contexts.MG: ...However, Natsuhi knew that he most often used this as an excuse for when he reluctantly went along with some deal that he just couldn't refuse.
contexts.UP: ...However, Natsuhi knew that he most often used this as an excuse after he couldn't bring himself to pass up a deal.

MG.japanese: 蔵臼は、義理を大事にしたいという美徳を掲げていた。…しかしそれは、断りきれない話を渋々承諾した際の言い訳にもっとも使われることを、夏妃は知っていた。
MG.translation: Krauss claimed to hold honor as a virtue. ...However, Natsuhi knew that he most often used this as an excuse for when he reluctantly went along with some deal that he just couldn't refuse.

UP.japanese: 蔵臼は、義理を大事にしたいという美徳を掲げていた。…しかしそれは、断りきれない話を渋々承諾した際の言い訳にもっとも使われることを、夏妃は知っていた。
UP.translation: Krauss claimed to hold honor as a virtue. ...However, Natsuhi knew that he most often used this as an excuse after he couldn't bring himself to pass up a deal.

findings.sourceReading: 断りきれない話を渋々承諾 explicitly combines inability to refuse with reluctant acceptance. OriginalPC7222–7223 and MG preserve reluctance.
findings.alternative: Unable to pass up can broadly describe inability to decline, but normally conveys an attractive opportunity and drops explicit reluctance; broader greed does not override this local motive.

findings.description: MG uses may gave been instead of may have been.

contexts.japanese: ……だからこそ、触法に対する抵抗感が少なかったのかもしれない。
contexts.japanesePS3: ……だからこそ、触法に対する抵抗感が少なかったのかもしれない。
contexts.MG: ...This may gave been the factor that lessened his resistance towards breaking a couple laws.
contexts.UP: ......This might have lessened his resistance towards breaking a couple laws.

MG.japanese: ……蔵臼は本気で、数々の事業が成功し、必ず大きな実りがあると信じていた。だから、多少、法に触れることになろうとも、すぐにそれを返済して、なかったことに出来ると信じていた。……だからこそ、触法に対する抵抗感が少なかったのかもしれない。
MG.translation: ...Krauss had seriously believed that he would succeed with several businesses...and that he would definitely gain huge profits. So, he had figured that even if he stepped over a few legal lines, he would be able to pay everything back before too long and pretend that the whole thing had never happened. ...This may gave been the factor that lessened his resistance towards breaking a couple laws.

UP.japanese: ……蔵臼は本気で、数々の事業が成功し、必ず大きな実りがあると信じていた。だから、多少、法に触れることになろうとも、すぐにそれを返済して、なかったことに出来ると信じていた。……だからこそ、触法に対する抵抗感が少なかったのかもしれない。
UP.translation: ......Krauss had seriously believed that his many projects would definitely succeed and return huge profits. So he had figured that even if he broke a few laws, he would be able to pay everything back before too long and pretend that the whole thing had never happened. ......This might have lessened his resistance towards breaking a couple laws.

findings.sourceReading: Modal perfect requires have been. OriginalPC7619 and UP use grammatical might have lessened.
findings.alternative: No deliberate dialect or interruption licenses gave after may.

findings.description: MG adds that nothing mattered to Krauss but survival where the Japanese describes heedless means of raising money.

contexts.japanese: 多額の金を捻出するために、形振り構わなかったということだろう。
contexts.japanesePS3: 多額の金を捻出するために、形振り構わなかったということだろう。
contexts.MG: He's probably been so intent on raising a large sum of money...that nothing had mattered to him but survival.
contexts.UP: He had probably been so intent on raising a large sum of money that he hadn't paid any heed to appearances.

MG.japanese: 刑事訴訟ということは、…何かの法に触れたということだ。多額の金を捻出するために、形振り構わなかったということだろう。
MG.translation: If it would come to criminal charges, ...then he must have broken some laws. He's probably been so intent on raising a large sum of money...that nothing had mattered to him but survival.

UP.japanese: 刑事訴訟ということは、…何かの法に触れたということだ。多額の金を捻出するために、形振り構わなかったということだろう。
UP.translation: If it would come to criminal charges, ...then he must have broken some laws. He had probably been so intent on raising a large sum of money that he hadn't paid any heed to appearances.

findings.sourceReading: 形振り構わなかった describes disregarding appearances or scruples in obtaining money. OriginalPC7607–7610 and UP preserve this.
findings.alternative: Financial survival can express desperation, but the exclusive survival motive is added and replaces the specified heedlessness toward means;322–324 instead explain expected venture profits.

findings.description: MG omits to from would not be able to solve it.

contexts.japanese: 解けるはずさ、解けないはずがないんだ…！
contexts.japanesePS3: 解けるはずさ、解けないはずがないんだ…！
contexts.MG: We should be able to solve it, ...and there's no reason we wouldn't be able solve it...!
contexts.UP: We should be able to solve it... There's no way we can't solve it...!

MG.japanese: 「そうだ、あんなの親父が作った気紛れななぞなぞなんだ…！！　解けるはずさ、解けないはずがないんだ…！　それしかないんだ！！」
MG.translation: Yes, it's a fanciful riddle that Father created...!! We should be able to solve it, ...and there's no reason we wouldn't be able solve it...! It's the only way!!"

UP.japanese: 「そうだ、あんなの親父が作った気紛れななぞなぞなんだ…！！　解けるはずさ、解けないはずがないんだ…！　それしかないんだ！！」
UP.translation: "Yes, it's just a fanciful little puzzle that Dad created...!! We should be able to solve it... There's no way we can't solve it...! It's the only way!!"

findings.sourceReading: Able requires the to infinitive here. OriginalPC7793 and UP use grammatical there is no way we cannot solve it.
findings.alternative: No deliberate dialect or interruption licenses omission of to.
